runbook: 1. Set MODELRIG_DEEPINFRA_API_KEY and/or MODELRIG_FIREWORKS_API_KEY in packages/modelrig/.env.local (and Render staging).
2. Verify exact host model ids against each host's live catalog (ids here follow the pricing map; hosts rename dated checkpoints).
3. Per target: npx modelrig-probes run --model <provider>/<model> (3 classes; budget-enveloped).
4. Rebuild registry (build-probed → build-registry → build-leaderboard → sync-registry-mirror) — parity-50 on the leaderboard moves automatically.
5. Add callNotes per model in src/registry/call-notes.ts as quirks surface.
6. New probed entries auto-feed the watch loop's new-model lane on later cycles.

7. MONTHLY (C4 finding F4 — standing operational step, not part of this campaign's one-shot run): re-render parity-50 against OpenRouter's current top-50. Run build-leaderboard + sync-registry-mirror and review registry/parity-50.json — the list churns, so a static 'X/50 probed' number silently rots. First refresh due ~2026-09-02; tracked as architect-queue item 6 in docs/ModelRig/todo-queue.md.

parity50_refresh.why: parity-50 is measured against a list that changes; an unrefreshed coverage number reads as progress it hasn't made.

id_repair.correction_note: The build-session verification pass reported 11 unresolved ids using family stem-matching. That method was too loose in one direction and too tight in the other: it invented irrelevant 'near matches' (e.g. Hermes-3 for a Nemotron target) and MISSED exact hosted models (Fireworks `kimi-k3`, DeepInfra `Qwen3-Coder-...-Turbo`, the whole hosted Gemma-4 and Qwen3.5 lines). This repair pass re-queried both catalogs per family with substring matching. Treat the earlier near-match list as superseded.
